requirements.evidence: routes/web.php:18-44 defines all 11 contract routes with the required methods and middleware; Login.php:22-43, Register.php:26-50, PasswordResetController.php:20-66, EmailVerificationController.php:14-41 and LogoutController.php:12-20 implement the flows; lang/pt_BR/ui.php:13,19,21 provides 'Entrar', 'Senha' and 'Esqueceu a senha?'. Small gaps: existing views are untouched although requirement 9 explicitly includes them, and PasswordResetController.php:22 returns a validation error, not a status flash, for a malformed e-mail.

conventions.evidence: Deviates from the project Livewire pattern `#[Validate] + $this->validate()`: Login.php:24-27 and Register.php:32-36 pass inline rule arrays, so the public input properties declare no `#[Validate]` rules. No CHANGELOG.md/docs update, although the conventions require keeping them in sync. Positives: named-route links in login.blade.php:41,48 and components/layouts/app.blade.php:20-33, named-route redirects everywhere, a reusable layout component, and `Password::defaults()` set once in AppServiceProvider.php:30.

security.evidence: Input is validated server-side (Login.php:24-27, Register.php:32-36, PasswordResetController.php:22-45); failed logins and registrations are rate-limited (Login.php:50-66, Register.php:57-73); successful logins regenerate the session (Login.php:40, Register.php:47); logout invalidates the session and rotates the CSRF token (LogoutController.php:16-17); password reset rotates remember_token (PasswordResetController.php:50-55); verification uses EmailVerificationRequest, so a tampered id gets 403 (EmailVerificationController.php:23-29); Blade output is escaped and forms carry @csrf.

tests.evidence: AuthFlowTest.php:23-73 covers locale, login success/failure and the e-mail+IP rate limit; :71-118 covers registration, validation and IP throttle; :120-130 covers logout and home guards; :132-153 covers forgot-password non-disclosure/throttle and the single-email reset form; :155-183 covers token rejection and remember_token rotation; :185-215 covers verification, tampering and resend; :217-227 guards against hardcoded view paths. Missing the Livewire-policy unauthorized-call and tamper tests for the public submit() actions.

simplicity.evidence: Direct implementation on top of Laravel's auth, password broker and EmailVerificationRequest; no service or repository layers. The rate-limit helper is duplicated in Login.php:50-66 and Register.php:57-73, and two layout files (layouts/app.blade.php:1-4 and components/layouts/app.blade.php) overlap, so one may be redundant.

readability.evidence: Clear translation-key names, small controller/component methods and consistent Bulma markup. Minor: PasswordResetController::request() is an ambiguous name for the GET handler (PasswordResetController.php:15), submit()/render() omit return types (Login.php:22,45; Register.php:26,52), and the 227-line test file mixes all flows.

scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the auth task: .env.example:1-8, phpunit.xml:22-23, routes/web.php:18-44, app/Models/User.php:15, AppServiceProvider.php:30, bootstrap/app.php:17-18, lang/en/ui.php and lang/pt_BR/ui.php, the auth/home views, the two layouts and one auth test file. No unrelated refactors or out-of-scope mail/Docker/SCSS/JS work.

issues.explanation: The project's Livewire pattern is `#[Validate]` on the public input properties plus `$this->validate()`; both components pass inline rule arrays instead, leaving `$email`, `$name`, `$password` and `$password_confirmation` without declarative validation rules.
The conventions require keeping CHANGELOG.md (under `[Unreleased]`) and the setup/structure docs in sync; the new routes, views and locale defaults add no documentation entry.

Requirement 9 applies the `route()`/no-hardcoded-`href`/`action` rule to every view including the existing ones, but no existing view is modified in the diff; if either page contains a root-relative link the guard test at AuthFlowTest.php:217-227 will fail.

The forgot-password POST validates the e-mail format before returning the uniform `status` flash, so a malformed address gets a validation error instead of the 'always answers with a status flash' response.

Login and register have happy-path, validation and rate-limit tests, but there is no unauthorized-call or tamper test for the public `submit()` actions, which the Livewire definition of done requires for each action.
This wrapper delegates to `components/layouts/app.blade.php`; since Livewire can use the component layout directly, the second layout file is likely redundant depending on the configured layout name.
`request()` is an ambiguous name for the GET forgot-password handler, and `submit()`/`render()` in the Livewire components omit return types, slightly reducing clarity.

review.summary: This change builds the complete session-auth flow in Livewire 4 and Bulma: login, registration, logout, home, forgot/reset password, e-mail verification, pt-BR/en UI translations, rate limiting and a broad Pest suite. It is secure and covers the main paths well; the review is held at approve-with-nits by the `#[Validate]` convention deviation, missing docs, missing Livewire unauthorized/tamper tests, and a few unverified or edge-case details.
